A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Value Anchoring study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, added and removed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-4 and Gemini Pro questionnaire experiments, including value rankings, Cronbach's alpha and MDS comparisons with human data.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds Llama and Gemma evaluations, anchored-response curves, and batch-versus-sequential prompting results.

M1.justification: The Value Anchor procedure and four alternative prompt templates remain unchanged. Additional models implement the same prompting approach; sequential administration is examined as an evaluation variant.

E1.justification: Both versions use the 57-item PVQ-RR covering 19 values and the human benchmark of 53,472 participants from 49 cultural groups. Additional model-generated responses and sequential administration remain within the same questionnaire task and population coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds the Basic prompt to the MDS comparison, whereas v1 Table 2 includes only Value Anchor, Demographic, Generated Persona and Names. Those comparators remain; 'Persona' is a shortened label for Generated Persona.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from GPT-4 and Gemini Pro to include Llama 3.1 8B/70B and Gemma 2 9B/27B. Appendix H adds sequential-versus-batch administration. Cronbach's alpha is removed, reducing the main evaluation from three metrics to two. The stated temperatures and 300-administration setup are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds anchored-score curves testing how neighboring and opposing values respond to an anchor (Section 4.1, Figure 4), and administration-sensitivity comparisons (Appendix H). It removes the within-value consistency analysis and its temperature-sensitivity evidence, previously presented in v1 Figures 3 and 6.

E5.justification: v1's reported Wilcoxon comparison, paired t-tests and Cronbach-alpha standard-deviation plots are removed. v3 Appendix H adds z statistics and p-values for batch-versus-sequential ranking comparisons. This substantially changes statistical reporting; neither version establishes additional independent repetitions or seed-based uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Shared GPT-4/Gemini per-prompt rankings and MDS scores remain unchanged. v3 adds results for four models, Basic-prompt MDS, anchored-response curves and sequential administration; Table 5 reports Llama 3.1 70B Value Anchor discrepancies of 0.10 for batch and 0.14 for serial prompting. Pooled-ranking and Cronbach-alpha results are removed.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, theoretical derivations or proofs are added or revised. The new anchoring explanation is empirical and qualitative. Removal of the standard Cronbach-alpha formula accompanies removal of that evaluation metric rather than a revision of mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims about prompt-dependent human-like value rankings and correlations remain. v3 additionally presents explaining anchoring-induced correlations as a contribution, emphasizes agreement across commercial and open models, and expands the stated persona-dataset contribution from two datasets to six.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds an explanation connecting anchor-centered score patterns to inter-value correlations, while acknowledging Gemma 2 9B's different behavior. Appendix H qualifies whether batch administration is preferable. The earlier interpretation that higher temperature compromises within-value consistency is removed; the questionnaire-specific applicability limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents output-parseability checks, reasons for unavailable Gemma 2 27B results, and Instruct model variants. The explicit random gender-assignment rule for ambiguous prompts disappears from the description, without establishing a procedural change. Code-access statements in Section 3 and Appendix A remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to earlier value, prompting and persona-evaluation research remain the same. Converting numbered citations to author-year citations does not change the research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain intact. Local rewrites clarify first- versus second-order statistics and revise the results discussion; subsection and appendix organization changes around the removed consistency analysis and new analyses. The author list and citation style also change.

P2.justification: Result displays are substantially reorganized: Figure 2 gains an expanded heatmap and ranking panel, the MDS table expands, and new anchoring, sequential-comparison and open-model displays appear. The pooled-ranking table and alpha charts disappear. Existing GPT-4/Gemini MDS plots are retained and consolidated, alongside changes to the document template.

improvement.justification: v3 better tests generality and administration sensitivity through open-model evaluations, the Basic-prompt MDS control and sequential prompting. Section 4.1 also strengthens interpretation. These gains are limited by removal of within-value reliability evidence and an unexplained discrepancy: Llama 3.1 8B Basic-prompt batch correlations at temperature zero are 0.80 in Figure 2a and 0.67 in Figure 6.
